title: Emission landmark stitcher for token cost and cache signals
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem: We currently surface token-level latency and cost as coarse aggregates; KV cache hits and micro-timing events are not reliably correlated with final billing/latency dashboards. This makes it hard to explain spikes, tune prefetching, or allocate cost to customers accurately.

Goal: Build an "emission landmark stitcher" that stitches sampled per-token micro-timings, cache-hit signals, and request metadata into queryable landmarks that map each emitted token (or subtoken) to contributing latency and cost signals across the serving stack. The stitcher produces an event stream compatible with our metrics/log pipeline and a compact per-request artifact for debugging and downstream billing reconciliation.

Approach summary:
- Instrument runtime to emit lightweight "landmark" markers at key points: prefetch completion, KV cache hit/miss, attention-kernel start/end, kernel-queue-wait, and token emission finalization. Each marker includes a small token-index slice, request id, model variant, and sequence offset.
- Use sampling for long requests (e.g., >256 tokens) to avoid excessive telemetry: deterministic reservoir sampling at request start so that landmarks are reproducible for reruns.
- Implement a stitcher service that ingests landmarks, correlates them by request id and token offset, computes per-landmark delta timings (ms) and cache signal attribution, and emits a stitched envelope per sampled token. The stitched envelopes are 1) fed into the metrics pipeline (Prometheus/OTLP) for aggregated dashboards and 2) stored in a low-cost long-term store (compressed logs) for audit and billing reconciliation.
- Provide an API to fetch the stitched artifact for a given request id and sampled offsets to power the console "token probe" UI and SRE debugging flows.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Telemetry volume vs. fidelity: default sampling keeps volume bounded; full-capture is opt-in for tenants on Dedicated.
- Stitcher latency: pipeline is mostly asynchronous; console UI will read from stores, not inline. Low-latency path exists for small requests to support live debugging.
- Privacy: emitted landmarks exclude raw prompt text and PII; only token indices and anonymized model metadata are included.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: billing ledger ingestion changes and visual console UX tweaks beyond the token-probe fetch API.
acceptance_criteria: Landmark events emitted at runtime for prefetch, KV hit/miss, kernel start/end, and emission finalization for all sampled requests.
Stitcher service ingests landmarks and produces stitched per-token envelopes with delta timings and cache-hit flags for sampled tokens.
Aggregated metrics (p50/p95/p99 per-token latency buckets) emitted to OTLP/metrics pipeline and visible on staging dashboard.
API endpoint to fetch stitched envelopes by request id and sampled offsets implemented and integrated with Console debug flow.
Telemetry volume under default sampling stays within agreed quota (+/-10%) during 24h load test.
Unit and integration tests for sampling determinism, stitch correctness, and graceful handling of partial/missing landmarks.
Design doc and data retention/format documented and linked in artifacts.
implementation_steps: Add lightweight landmark emission hooks in serving runtime (C++/Rust) with schema v1 (request_id, offset, marker_type, ts_ms, model_tag, seq_len_hint).
Implement deterministic reservoir sampler at request start and pass sampling decision through request context.
Create stitcher prototype (Go) that consumes landmarks via existing OTLP/ingestion topic and assembles stitched envelopes keyed by request_id + offset.
Define envelope schema and compression format (ndjson + gzip) and wire into existing logs bucket with retention policy.
Expose read API (internal) to fetch stitched artifacts; add auth checks and rate limits.
Emit aggregated metrics from stitcher (per-token latency histograms, cache-hit ratios) to metrics pipeline.
Load test and measure telemetry volume; iterate sampler thresholds to meet quota targets.
Create Confluence design doc and sample Console integration PR linking to API contract.
testing_plan: Unit tests for landmark serialization/deserialization and timestamp ordering invariants.
Deterministic sampling tests (same seed/headers -> identical sampling decisions).
Integration test: run local runtime + stitcher with synthetic requests (various lengths) and assert stitched envelopes match ground-truth timing deltas.
Stress test ingesting landmarks at 2x peak QPS for 1 hour; validate shard/backpressure behavior.
Staging rollout: enable default sampling + console fetch API for internal teams and collect feedback for 2 weeks.
Postmortem checklist: if telemetry gaps observed, add fallbacks to rehydrate from trace spans.
telemetry_queries: console query:select * from stitched_envelopes where request_id = '<example>' limit 100
dashboards: token_probes.staging (p50/p95/p99 prefetch vs kernel vs emission)
comments: 2026-02-25 - Aisha Banerjee: Created ticket after spike that compared KV-prefetch counters to billing anomalies. Summary attached in Confluence.
2026-03-01 - Marco Li: Implemented initial runtime hook prototype and validated low overhead in microbenchmarks (~0.3% p99 increase on small models).
2026-03-04 - Design review (Emily Chen): Approved schema v1 with privacy guardrails; requested explicit field list and no prompt text in events.
2026-03-07 - Marco Li: Stitcher prototype ingesting landmarks from OTLP exporter; currently keeps in-memory partial windows keyed by request_id. Working through eviction policy for large requests.
2026-03-10 - QA (Ravi Patel): Added integration tests for sampling determinism; found bug where sampling seed wasn't propagated for streamed responses — fix in PR #7210.
2026-03-12 - PM (Sofia Alvarez): Prioritized read API + dashboard surface for cycle demo. Flagging potential ops cost if Dedicated tenants opt into full-capture.
Next steps: finish compression + long-term storage wiring, finalize metrics dashboard panels, schedule staging rollout and 72h smoke.
